title: Why are men OBSESSED with American Psycho?
summary: A narrated analysis of American Psycho in which Patrick Bateman stands for modern society: masked identity, appearance-obsessed masculinity, materialism, porn-driven objectification of women and repressed male anger. He argues young men relate to Bateman because he is what society tells them to become, and watching him is a cathartic outlet for their own civilizational anxiety.
claims: Bateman became an alpha-male meme icon because he embodies what society tells men to be (handsome, muscular, rich), which is entirely surface-level
Modern culture reduces fitness and self-improvement to materialistic means without deeper spirituality
Bateman's morning routine is a desperate re-application of a fake identity, not the schedule of a balanced man
Everyone has to wear a social mask, but today many men feel they must be someone else entirely to exist
Male power fantasies once served as blueprints for masculinity; modern pop-culture memes only work as substitutes
The film satirises marriage reduced to a materialistic system without love, each act motivated by personal gain
A society that demonises outward anger produces overgrown boys with poor anger management; the only way to master an emotion is to experience it fully and regularly
Antisocial personality traits are androgenic traits taken to the extreme, which is why males are overrepresented
Constant porn and music keep dopamine high as coping mechanisms that distract from conscience
Men who ignore those who can't raise their status, and are desperate to look too cool, are themselves needy for validation and fragile
The business card scene shows modern men judging their worth by possessions; identity has been replaced by things they can buy
Most humans are deathly afraid of ridicule, as Bateman is
Treating violent male acts only as gore ignores their causes and leaves society unprepared for their return
Bateman's view of women as bodies to use mirrors the modern bachelor's porn-shaped, resentful attraction; you can't cherish what you don't understand
Porn plays a central role in destroying masculinity by objectifying the female body and erasing male respect for it
Bateman's fascination for a generation without male role models comes from him being hypermasculinity driven by instinct without empathy
Jean is the only woman who escapes Bateman, because of her modesty, which he reads as symbolic of promiscuity being a trap for modern women
Bateman represents the spirit of modernity itself; there is no single psycho, everyone in the film is touched by it
